full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: This Rule by the opposite party No.l-petitioner directed against order No.4 dated 13-9-2005 passed by the learned District Judge; Dhaka in transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 918 of 2005 allowing the said case and there by transferring Artha Jari Case Nos. 30 or 2005 and 31 of 2005 from the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No.3. Dhaka to the Bankruptcy Court, Dhaka and order No.6 dated 18-9-2005 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 918 of 2005 rejecting an application tiled by the opposite party No.1 petitioner under section 151 or The Code of Civil Procedure. 

 3. These suits were decreed and consequently plaintiff filed the aforesaid execution cases. 

 4. In the aforementioned Artha Jari Cases opposite party No. 1 filed application for staying holding of auction sale and opposite party No. 1 having appointed as receiver by Bankruptcy Court, filed another application stating that Industrial Development Leasing Company of Bangladesh filed Bankruptcy Case in Bankruptcy Court against opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 as such the execution cases should be transferred to Bankruptcy Court. 

 6. On 16-7-2005 opposite party No. 1 filed similar application again for transferring the execution case to Bankruptcy Court as Industrial Development Leasing Company as plaintiff has filed Bankruptcy Case No. 5 of 2003 against opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 for declaring the Directors or till Company as bankrupt. Petitioner tiled application for time for filing written objection. Learned Judge fixed 13-9-2005 as it appears for service return but while the petitioner went for filing written objection. it was informed that the learned Judge has already allowed the application. 

 7. Learned District Judge by the impugned order transferred the cases by an non-speaking order as: 

 8. Mr. AQM Safiullah, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that, the order passed by the learned Joint District Judge is bad in law on two counts i.e. order is a non-speaking order and also that, any case and Artha Jari Case filed before any Artha Rin Adalat it cannot be transferred to any other Court excepting from one Artha Rin Adalat to another, as such, the order passed by the learned Joint District Judge transferring the case to Bankruptcy Court having been passed beyond his jurisdiction liable to be set aside. 

 9. Mr. AQM. Safiullah, the learned Advocate for the petitioner in this subject matter, relied on the decision of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation vs Shahid Sarwar Abu Hossain. 9 BLT 289 = 6 BLC 751 wherein similar question was posted and it was held that the provisions of one special law cannot over-rided the provisions of another special law as such, transfer of a case filed under Artha Rin Adalat to Bankruptcy Court is not proper and legal. 

 11. Under section 109 of Bankruptcy Act, the learned District Judge has power to transfer and withdraw any proceeding pending in subordinate Court to himself or to any subordinate Court but it relates only to the proceeding under Bankruptcy Act but the learned District Judge has no power to transfer any suit-under Artha Rin Adalat Ain to the Court who is specially meant for Bankruptcy Act to be heard and disposed of with Bankruptcy proceeding. In that case the learned District Judge exceed his jurisdiction. The learned Judge can transfer a suit or Artha Rin Adalat to any subordinate Judge, even to a subordinate Judge holding jurisdiction to try Bankruptcy proceedings but transferee Court cannot proceed the suit under Bankruptcy Act as Artha Rin Adalat Ain itself has provision to deal with the suits under the Ain. Artha Rin Adalat Ain also provides for transfer under sections 4 and 5 empowering the District Judge to transfer suits of Artha Rin Ain from one Court to another having jurisdiction to deal with Artha Rin cases, not to any other Court. Since the laws are special laws having provided for special remedies as such, case or suit of one jurisdiction cannot be heard and disposed of by another jurisdiction because in that case one of the jurisdiction become disqualified and subordinate to the other jurisdiction which cannot be done or it is not the intents of the legislature. One special law cannot he subordinate to other subordinate law. When there is conflict of law then it will be decided on the basis or the law under which the suit or proceeding initiated. It may be further said cases under Bankruptcy Act are proceeding where cases under Artha Rin Adalat Ain are suits. 

 12. Our Appellate Division in the case or House Building Finance Corporation vs Jahanura Begum. 16 BLD (AD) 231 = 49 DLR (AD) 80 held that House Building Finance Corporation Order. PO 7 of 1973 having provides for remedy in itself the cases under PO 7 of 1973 cannot be transferred to Artha Rin Adalat. 

 13. Considering all these aspects of the case, we are satisfied that the impugned order suffers from patent illegality and liable to be set aside.
